description: Predicate 4c SAT — channel-economics resilience. Three channel-investment options (linkedin_30k, content_30k, no_invest) with different base CACs (80 / 60 / 100). Two competitors can each play 3 counter-response postures (full counter / partial / no counter). LinkedIn is easy for competitors to counter-bid (CAC lifts of 25-30 each); content compounds and is hard to counter (lifts of 4-8); no_invest drifts slightly (1-5). With target_cac=85 (LTV ceiling), only content_30k stays under 85 across all 9 combos worst-case (60 + 8 + 6 = 74). LinkedIn blows out (80 + 30 + 25 = 135); no_invest blows out under any meaningful counter (100 + anything > 85). Unique durable winner: content_30k.
_solver_note: Manual skolemization over response combos (3 x 3 = 9). CAC inequality: my_cac_after_move[i] + sum(competitor_counter_impact[i][k][response_k]) <= target_cac, evaluated for the chosen move i. content_30k worst case: 60 + 8 + 6 = 74 <= 85. linkedin_30k worst case: 80 + 30 + 25 = 135 (kill). no_invest worst case: 100 + 5 + 4 = 109 (kill, and no_invest's base CAC alone exceeds the ceiling).
